title: BrlProduction
description: Production BANZA Revocation List (BRL). Enumerates revoked cryptographic material — delegated keys, releases and artifacts — in the trust path. Revocation is a security signal over material, never an entity-level sanction (ADR-027/040). FAIL-CLOSED SEMANTICS: a verifier that cannot fetch, parse, or verify the signature of a current, non-expired BRL MUST treat trust as revoked (deny), never as granted. A stale (expired) BRL is a hard failure. An empty 'revoked' array means nothing is revoked, NOT that verification may be skipped. Publishing a BRL does not move funds and does not make BANZA a payment processor; BANZA is an open protocol. At M2_PROTOCOL_IMPLEMENTATION the BRL is prepared-but-gated and signed only after the offline root-key ceremony.
_boundary: Production of the BANZA protocol, not financial production. BANZA is an open protocol; it does not process payments, settle value, or move funds. Licence/authorisation belongs to the operator, not to BANZA.

issuer.description: Issuer of the revocation list: the BANZA protocol trust root.

issued_at.description: Issuance timestamp. Verifiers reject BRLs with issued_at in the future.

expires_at.description: Expiry timestamp. A BRL past expires_at is stale and MUST be treated as a hard fail-closed failure.

revoked.description: Revoked entries. Empty array means nothing revoked (still requires a valid, non-expired, verified BRL).

operator_id.description: Operator whose key material is affected (context only; revocation targets the material named by revoked_ref, not the entity).

permanent.description: True if the revocation is permanent and non-reversible.

revoked_ref.description: Identifier of the revoked cryptographic material — a delegated key id, release id, or artifact id — when applicable.

signature_ref.description: Reference to the detached signature over the canonical BRL bytes, produced by a BANZA revocation-domain key. Verification is mandatory (fail-closed).
